passages.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man makes plans in his heart.
He decides what he wants to do.
But the LORD gives the answer of the tongue.
God controls what is finally spoken.
God has the final word.
passages.original: לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי־ לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man sees his own ways as pure.
He believes his actions are right.
The LORD examines his motives.
The LORD judges what is in his heart.
passages.original: כָּֽל־ דַּרְכֵי־ אִ֭ישׁ זַ֣ךְ בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן רוּח֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He rules over all things.
Give your actions to the LORD.
Trust Him with what you do.
He will make your plans succeed.
He will guide your thoughts and efforts.
He will bring your plans to completion.
passages.original: גֹּ֣ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וְ֝יִכֹּ֗נוּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.
passages.sermon: The LORD made everything for His purpose.\r\nHe made the wicked for the day of disaster.
passages.original: כֹּ֤ל פָּעַ֣ל יְ֭הוָה לַֽמַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ וְגַם־ רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לְי֣וֹם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
passages.sermon:
The LORD hates everyone who is proud in heart.
A proud person is detestable to the LORD.
God will not let the proud go unpunished.
No one who is proud will escape punishment.
passages.original: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה כָּל־ גְּבַהּ־ לֵ֑ב יָ֥ד לְ֝יָ֗ד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃

passages.text: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
passages.sermon: God forgives sin through loving devotion and faithfulness.\r\nA person turns away from evil by fearing the LORD.
passages.original: בְּחֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יְכֻפַּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע׃

passages.text: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has power over all people.
A man can live in a way that pleases the LORD.
When a man pleases the LORD, the LORD acts.
The LORD brings peace to the man.
The LORD causes even the man’s enemies to live at peace with him.
passages.original: בִּרְצ֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ גַּם־ א֝וֹיְבָ֗יו יַשְׁלִ֥ם אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
passages.sermon:
Righteousness is good.
A small amount with righteousness is better.
Great gain without justice is not better.
Having little with righteousness is better than having much with injustice.
passages.original: טוֹב־ מְ֭עַט בִּצְדָקָ֑ה מֵרֹ֥ב תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
passages.sermon:
A man thinks about his path.
He makes plans in his heart.
The LORD decides where he will go.
The LORD directs his steps.
passages.original: לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.
passages.sermon:
A king speaks with authority from God.
His words carry a divine verdict.
A king must speak with justice.
He must not betray what is right.
passages.original: קֶ֤סֶם׀ עַֽל־ שִׂפְתֵי־ מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל־ פִּֽיו׃

passages.text: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gives honest scales and balances.
He cares about every weight in the bag.
He makes sure all measures are fair.
He wants justice in every transaction.
passages.original: פֶּ֤לֶס׀ וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל־ אַבְנֵי־ כִֽיס׃

passages.text: Wicked behavior is detestable to kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
passages.sermon:
A king hates wicked behavior.
A king finds evil actions detestable.
A king wants righteousness.
Righteousness makes a throne secure.
A throne stands firm through justice.
passages.original: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.
passages.sermon: A king delights in righteous words.\r\nA king loves a person who speaks honestly.
passages.original: רְצ֣וֹן מְ֭לָכִים שִׂפְתֵי־ צֶ֑דֶק וְדֹבֵ֖ר יְשָׁרִ֣ים יֶאֱהָֽב׃

passages.text: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
passages.sermon:
A king is a ruler with great power.
A king’s anger brings deadly danger.
His wrath acts like a messenger of death.
A wise man can calm the king’s anger.
A wise man brings peace and safety.
passages.original: חֲמַת־ מֶ֥לֶךְ מַלְאֲכֵי־ מָ֑וֶת וְאִ֖ישׁ חָכָ֣ם יְכַפְּרֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
passages.sermon:
A king is a ruler.
A king’s face can shine with joy or approval.
When a king’s face shines, people receive life.
A king’s favor brings blessing.
His favor is like a spring rain cloud.
A spring rain cloud brings refreshment and growth.
passages.original: בְּאוֹר־ פְּנֵי־ מֶ֥לֶךְ חַיִּ֑ים וּ֝רְצוֹנ֗וֹ כְּעָ֣ב מַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is better than gold.
Understanding is more desirable than silver.
It is good to seek wisdom.
It is better to gain understanding than to seek riches.
passages.original: קְֽנֹה־ חָכְמָ֗ה מַה־ טּ֥וֹב מֵחָר֑וּץ וּקְנ֥וֹת בִּ֝ינָ֗ה נִבְחָ֥ר מִכָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.
passages.sermon:
The upright person chooses a straight path.
This path turns away from evil.
A person who guards his way stays safe.
He protects his own life by doing this.
passages.original: מְסִלַּ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים ס֣וּר מֵרָ֑ע שֹׁמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ נֹצֵ֥ר דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
passages.sermon:
Pride comes before destruction.
A proud person will be destroyed.
A haughty spirit comes before a fall.
A person with a haughty spirit will fall.
passages.original: לִפְנֵי־ שֶׁ֥בֶר גָּא֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י כִ֝שָּׁל֗וֹן גֹּ֣בַהּ רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.
passages.sermon:
A person who is lowly in spirit is humble.
A humble person chooses to be with other humble people.
It is better to be humble with the poor.
It is not good to share riches with the proud.
Being humble is better than being proud, even if the proud have wealth.
passages.original: ט֣וֹב שְׁפַל־ ר֭וּחַ אֶת־ עֲנִיִּים מֵֽחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁ֝לָ֗ל אֶת־ גֵּאִֽים׃

passages.text: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
passages.sermon: A person who listens to instruction will find good things.\r\nA person who trusts in the LORD is blessed.
passages.original: מַשְׂכִּ֣יל עַל־ דָּ֭בָר יִמְצָא־ ט֑וֹב וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה אַשְׁרָֽיו׃

passages.text: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
passages.sermon:
A person with a wise heart is called discerning.
Pleasant speech helps people learn.
Pleasant words make instruction easier.
People value those who speak kindly and teach well.
passages.original: לַחֲכַם־ לֵ֭ב יִקָּרֵ֣א נָב֑וֹן וּמֶ֥תֶק שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יֹסִ֥יף לֶֽקַח׃

passages.text: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
passages.sermon:
Understanding gives life to the person who has it.
Understanding is like a fountain that brings life.
Fools receive discipline.
The discipline of fools is foolishness.
Fools do not gain wisdom from correction.
Their discipline does not help them.
passages.original: מְק֣וֹר חַ֭יִּים שֵׂ֣כֶל בְּעָלָ֑יו וּמוּסַ֖ר אֱוִלִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
passages.sermon:
A wise man has a wise heart.
His heart teaches his mouth.
His heart helps him speak well.
His lips become more persuasive because of his wise heart.
passages.original: לֵ֣ב חָ֭כָם יַשְׂכִּ֣יל פִּ֑יהוּ וְעַל־ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו יֹסִ֥יף לֶֽקַח׃

passages.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
passages.sermon: Pleasant words are like honeycomb.\r\nPleasant words taste sweet to the soul.\r\nPleasant words bring healing to the bones.
passages.original: צוּף־ דְּ֭בַשׁ אִמְרֵי־ נֹ֑עַם מָת֥וֹק לַ֝נֶּפֶשׁ וּמַרְפֵּ֥א לָעָֽצֶם׃

passages.text: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
passages.sermon: A man may see a path before him.\r\nThis path may look right to him.\r\nBut the end of this path leads to death.
passages.original: יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־ מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.
passages.sermon:
A worker feels hunger.
This hunger belongs to him.
His hunger pushes him to work.
His appetite gives him energy.
His need for food drives him forward.
He works because he wants to satisfy his hunger.
passages.original: נֶ֣פֶשׁ עָ֭מֵל עָ֣מְלָה לּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ אָכַ֖ף עָלָ֣יו פִּֽיהוּ׃

passages.text: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
passages.sermon:
A worthless man looks for evil.
He tries to find ways to do harm.
His words burn like a scorching fire.
His speech causes pain and destruction.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ בְּ֭לִיַּעַל כֹּרֶ֣ה רָעָ֑ה וְעַל־ שְׂפָתָיו כְּאֵ֣שׁ צָרָֽבֶת׃

passages.text: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
passages.sermon:
A perverse man spreads dissension.
He causes conflict among people.
A gossip divides close friends.
He separates those who were once close.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת יְשַׁלַּ֣ח מָד֑וֹן וְ֝נִרְגָּ֗ן מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃

passages.text: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
passages.sermon:
A violent man acts with cruelty.
He tempts his neighbor.
He leads his neighbor.
He takes his neighbor down a wrong path.
This path is not good.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ חָ֭מָס יְפַתֶּ֣ה רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝הוֹלִיכ֗וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
passages.sermon:
A person who winks his eye plans to do wrong.
He thinks about twisted and dishonest things.
A person who purses his lips is determined to do evil.
He is set on causing harm.
passages.original: עֹצֶ֣ה עֵ֭ינָיו לַחְשֹׁ֣ב תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת קֹרֵ֥ץ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו כִּלָּ֥ה רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Gray hair shows honor and dignity.
Gray hair is a crown of glory.
A person receives gray hair by living righteously.
A person finds this honor on the path of righteousness.
passages.original: עֲטֶ֣רֶת תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת שֵׂיבָ֑ה בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ צְ֝דָקָ֗ה תִּמָּצֵֽא׃

passages.text: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
passages.sermon: A person who is slow to anger is better than a strong warrior.\r\nA person who controls his temper is greater than someone who captures a city.
passages.original: ט֤וֹב אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם מִגִּבּ֑וֹר וּמֹשֵׁ֥ל בְּ֝רוּח֗וֹ מִלֹּכֵ֥ד עִֽיר׃

passages.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God controls all decisions.
People cast lots into their lap.
God determines the outcome of every lot.
No decision from casting lots happens apart from God.
God rules over chance and fate.
passages.original: בַּ֭חֵיק יוּטַ֣ל אֶת־ הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה כָּל־ מִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ׃
